exp1.finding: Real per-stage timing contradicts the fabricated fixed-fraction breakdown: on the sensitive path the Fabric commit (peer-CLI invoke: subprocess spawn + endorse/order/commit) dominates end-to-end latency, NOT the Ethereum anchor. Public (Ethereum-only) path is ~20x faster. Throughput is bounded by the serial Fabric commit on the sensitive path.

exp3.conclusion: Single-record anchoring costs ~273695 gas/record (measured). Merkle-batching amortizes one ~273623-gas root-anchor tx across the batch, so gas/record falls as 1/N -> at N=200 the reduction is 99.5%. All values are real receipt.gasUsed.

exp4.versioning_model: full-snapshot: deepcopy of entire state per version
exp4.rollback_model: get_version() linear O(n) scan from front + deepcopy(state)
exp4.conclusion: Rollback latency grows with the TARGET version's position in the history (get_version does a linear scan from the front) plus a full-state deepcopy. It is NOT O(1). Storage grows linearly with version count (full snapshots, no delta encoding). Absolute latencies are sub-millisecond at this scale, so a bounded-recovery claim is defensible, but the O(1) label is not.

exp5.note: Verified via REAL Ethereum tx hashes returned by the live orchestrator over 71 requests. Duplicates (sequential and concurrent) collapse to exactly one on-chain anchor via the content-hash idempotency slot; distinct requests each get a unique anchor. Orchestrator crash-recovery is a separate test requiring process-kill mid-commit and is noted as future hardening, not claimed here.

exp7.data_source: real twin_manager version deltas (deterministic multi-class workload)
exp7.finding: Block-level compression of REAL twin_manager version deltas reaches ~11.5x (uniform zlib-6). Per-class codec selection (HADC) improves on uniform by 6.2%. Classes selected DIFFERENT codecs, supporting the heterogeneity thesis.

provenance.data_source: real twin_manager version histories built in exp8_recovery_strategy.py:build_history(); deltas derived from consecutive real snapshots
provenance.implementation_note: twin_manager stores FULL SNAPSHOTS only — no checkpoint interval, no delta store, no inverse-delta application. Both recovery strategies are implemented in THIS EXPERIMENT, not in the production twin manager. Algorithm 2's branching must NOT be described as implemented in twin_manager.

eq36_validation.conclusion: Eq (36) u = min{n-k, q} is VALID AS AN UPPER BOUND and INVALID AS AN EQUALITY. Checkpoint restore costs (k mod q) delta applications, not q; q is the supremum over k, attained only in the worst case. The exact cost is u = min{n-k, k mod q}. The manuscript should state Eq (36) as u <= min{n-k, q}, or replace it with the exact form.
